title: Riemannian Gradient Descent for Gaussian Mixture Models with unknown diagonal covariances
summary: This paper investigates the numerical resolution of the Beurling-LASSO (BLASSO), a convex optimization framework that promotes sparsity in the space of measures. We consider its application to the estimation of Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) with an unknown number of components and unknown diagonal covariance matrices. Our approach combines the Conic Particle Gradient Descent (CPGD) principle with Riemannian gradient descent, to account for the underlying Fisher-Rao geometry of Gaussian distributions.
